class.name: HTTPServer
class.brief_description: A node that hosts an HTTP server.
class.description: Listens for plain HTTP requests, parses them, and resolves each one in a fixed order: a directory mounted with [method mount_files] is tried first, then a handler registered with [method route], then the [signal request_received] signal, and a request nothing answered is finally served [code]404 Not Found[/code]. Handlers and receivers alike are given a [code skip-lint]foundry.http.server.HTTPRequest[/code] describing the request and a [code skip-lint]foundry.http.server.HTTPResponse[/code] to complete. All work happens on the thread that drives the server. While the node is inside the scene tree it polls itself every frame; a headless caller can call [method poll] directly instead. Each connection currently serves exactly one request and is then closed. [b]Note:[/b] The default bind address is the loopback interface, so the server is reachable only from the local machine unless another address is passed to [method listen]. This class lives in the [code]foundry.http.server[/code] namespace, so it is reached either by its fully qualified name [code skip-lint]foundry.http.server.HTTPServer[/code] or, after [code]import foundry.http.server[/code], by the bare name [code]HTTPServer[/code]. Without that import the bare name does not resolve.

method.name: get_listening_port
method.description: Returns the port the server is bound to, or [code]-1[/code] if it is not listening. Use this to discover the port chosen by the operating system after calling [method listen] with port [code]0[/code].

method.name: is_listening
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while the server holds an open listening socket.

method.name: listen
method.description: Opens a listening socket on [member port] at [member bind_address] and returns [constant @GlobalScope.OK] on success. Set [member port] to [code]0[/code] to let the operating system pick a free port, then read it back with [method get_listening_port]. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_ALREADY_IN_USE] if the server is already listening, and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] if [member bind_address] cannot be parsed.

method.name: mount_files
method.description: Serves the files under [param root_dir] for every request path that starts with [param url_prefix]. [param url_prefix] must start with [code]/[/code], and a trailing [code]/[/code] on it is ignored, so [code]"/app"[/code] and [code]"/app/"[/code] mount the same way. The prefix only matches whole path segments, so [code]"/app"[/code] claims [code]/app/index.html[/code] but not [code]/application/index.html[/code]. [param root_dir] must name a readable directory; [code]res://[/code] and [code]user://[/code] paths are resolved to their location on disk. A registration that does not meet these conditions is rejected and no mount is added. A mount is resolved before any route, so a route can never shadow a file the mount holds. A path the mount holds no file for — including a directory — is left to the rest of the resolution: routes, then [signal request_received], then [code]404 Not Found[/code]. Only [code]GET[/code] and [code]HEAD[/code] are answered; any other method is refused with [code]405 Method Not Allowed[/code]. Responses carry a content type derived from the file extension, an [code]ETag[/code] and a [code]Last-Modified[/code] field. A request repeating either validator through [code]If-None-Match[/code] or [code]If-Modified-Since[/code] is answered with [code]304 Not Modified[/code], and a single [code skip-lint]Range[/code] request is answered with [code]206 Partial Content[/code], or [code]416 Range Not Satisfiable[/code] when the range lies past the end of the file. A request whose path resolves outside [param root_dir], whether through [code]..[/code], percent-escapes, an empty path segment, or a symbolic link leaving the directory, is answered with [code]403 Forbidden[/code] and the file is never opened. A path carrying a backslash or an escaped control character is refused the same way, so a request can never name one file and reach another. Such a request is refused whether or not anything exists at the escaping path, so a mount cannot be used to probe the rest of the filesystem, and the refusal is final: it never falls through to a route or to [signal request_received]. If several mounts match a path, the first one registered claims it.

method.name: poll
method.description: Accepts pending connections, parses whatever arrived, dispatches completed requests and writes pending responses. Called automatically once per frame while the node is inside the scene tree. Does nothing if the server is not listening.

method.name: route
method.description: Registers [param handler] for requests whose method equals [param method] and whose path equals [param path] exactly, with the query string excluded. [param method] is matched case-insensitively; [param path] must start with [code]/[/code]. The handler is called with the request and the response as its two arguments. If several handlers are registered for the same method and path, the first registration wins. A routed request does not reach [signal request_received] unless [member emit_for_all] is enabled.

method.name: stop
method.description: Closes the listening socket and every open connection. Does nothing if the server is not listening.

members.member: The address [method listen] binds to. Defaults to the loopback interface, so the server is reachable only from the local machine. Use [code]"*"[/code] to accept connections on every interface. An empty value is rejected and leaves the property unchanged.

If [code]true[/code], [signal request_received] is emitted for every request, including the ones a route already handled. Receivers then run after the route handler, so the response is usually already committed, and a receiver that tries to complete it again is refused: the body, the status and the header fields are all fixed at that point. Such a receiver is an observer of routed traffic, not a second author of the response. If [code]false[/code], the signal is emitted only for requests no route claimed, which keeps routed traffic off the signal.

The TCP port [method listen] binds to. Must be between [code]0[/code] and [code]65535[/code]; values outside that range are rejected and leave the property unchanged. [code]0[/code] asks the operating system for a free port.

signal.name: request_received
signal.description: Emitted for a request no route claimed, and for every request once [member emit_for_all] is enabled. A receiver completes [param response] the same way a route handler does; if none of them does, the request is answered with [code]404 Not Found[/code].
